judgements.justification: B's area chair rejected on its own view that the rewrite was 'a major revision', below final ratings 6, 6, 6, 5 and Reviewer_ATkA's 'polishing' and 'will not oppose accepting'; the chair posted nothing in the discussion.
Neither committee rested its recommendation on a forecast of broad impact.
The rebuttal raised scores in both committees (e4Tf in A; ATkA, f5mJ and 69AE in B), so it did not move one committee alone.
Only one B review (69AE) was inattentive; ATkA, f5mJ and VPWz engaged in detail, so B's scores do not rest on less scrutiny than A's.
Only B raised exact reconstruction as degenerate for a variational model, and B's meta-review made it its main reason; only B noted the single unrepeated CelebA run.

Both committees saw the overclaiming beyond Theorem 4 and the reliance on Dai and Wipf (2019); A's area chair asked for 'slightly more careful quantification', B's called it 'a serious issue for a theoretical work'.
Reviewer_f5mJ raised to 6 after reading the others' exchanges, but that moved B toward A, not away.
No reviewer's rating clearly contradicts their own text; 69AE's 5 matches its remaining doubt on VAE relevance.
No B reviewer said they could not judge the paper; ATkA's reserve was about unseen revisions, not ability to judge.
B's meta-review leans on Reviewer_69AE, the lone 5, and adopts its zero-reconstruction objection as its main reason although ATkA explicitly disagreed with it.
B's reviewers raised the framing as central objections, not the questions A asked, so the verbal assessments were not similar.
A's spotlight came with an 8 from Reviewer_e4Tf, and B's spread came at a lower mean (5.75 against 7.33).
A's e4Tf raised to 8 and A's area chair accepted the Theorem 4 extension on promised text changes nobody saw; B's ATkA declined a high score without seeing the revision.
A's meta-review carried forward its reviewers' and its own reservations (overclaiming, 'sparse', long introduction).
B's meta-review limits the result to 'a Gaussian likelihood with a learned variance', but Theorem 4 covers any penalty h; 69AE's 'firm no' also rested on two wrong claims (PCA, overfitting).
Both committees saw concessions paired with fixes and both raised scores, so no committee alone ended higher than its information supported.
No objection in either committee came after the authors could answer it.
The committees' scores differ (7, 7, 8 against 6, 6, 6, 5), so the split is not a tier cut-off on near-identical reviews.
B's area chair followed its highest-confidence reviewer (69AE, confidence 5) rather than passing over it.
The rebuttal lifted B's scores as much as A's; B's area chair, not the reviewers, judged the concerns beyond a response.
Without 69AE's 5, B's remaining 6, 6, 6 still do not match A's 7, 7, 8.
Reviewer_69AE posted in the discussion and adjusted its score, though it left one reply unanswered.
No area chair set aside a detractor and defended acceptance against it.
Neither committee raised audience breadth or venue fit.
B's meta-review says the reviewers 'were not convinced' on VAE applicability, but only 69AE held that view, and it calls 'a major revision' what ATkA called 'polishing'.
Most reviewers in both committees replied to the response.
A's reviewers rated at confidence 4 and did not say they could not verify the results.
B's reviewers did not split evenly between accept and reject; three rated 6 and one 5.
The authors answered different questions in each committee, but gave no conflicting accounts; both got the extension to a separate g.
A's judgement that the work is well distinguished from Dai and Wipf (2019) is not shown to be wrong; B only wanted a dedicated comparison.
A's spotlight matches its scores (7, 7, 8 at confidence 4), even though the meta-review gives no tier reason beyond 'a strong paper'.

added.name: Neighbouring-field reviewers contested the paper's framing
added.definition: One committee's critical reviewers read the paper from the premises of a neighbouring field and objected to its framing or definitions on those premises, not to its technical results, while the other committee's reviewers accepted the paper's framing, and those framing objections counted against the paper.
added.justification: R05 says only one committee raised a concern, and R06 covers different weight on a shared one; neither names the cause here, that B's critics judged the framing from another field's premises (VI, information bottleneck), which ATkA itself said was 'not about the particular technical findings but about the main narrative'.

reasoning: Both committees found the theory correct and saw the same overclaiming. The split comes from B's area chair: it ruled the rewrite a major revision against borderline-positive final ratings, adopted the lone detractor's VAE objection as the reviewers' shared view, and misstated the scope of Theorem 4 (R01, R10, R25, R15). A tolerated the overclaiming and raised on promised edits (R06, R13). Only B raised the variational-model and experiment concerns (R05). One new reason covers the framing objections that B's critics brought from neighbouring fields.
